Main.sentence: Kenneth Lee Salazar (born March 2, 1955) is an American lawyer, politician, and diplomat who served as ___E:United States ambassador to Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Mexico)___ from 2021 to 2025.  He previously served as the 50th ___E:United States Secretary of the Interior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Interior)___ in the administration of ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ from 2009 to 2013. A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , he previously was a ___E:United States Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ from ___E:Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado)___ from 2005 to 2009.

Salazar served as ___E:Attorney General of Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_General_of_Colorado)___ from 1999 to 2005. He became the first Latino Senator representing Colorado in 2005. He and ___E:Mel Martínez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Mart%C3%ADnez)___ ( ___E:R U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Republican_Party)___ - ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ ) were the first ___E:Hispanic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans)___ U.S. senators since 1977; they were joined by ___E:Bob Menendez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Menendez)___ (D- ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ ) in 2006.
On December 17, 2008, President-elect Obama announced he would nominate Salazar as U.S. secretary of the interior.
The ___E:environmentalist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmentalism)___ movement's [vague] reaction to this nomination was mixed.

Previously, Salazar supported the nomination of ___E:Gale Norton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gale_Norton)___ to Secretary of the Interior,  President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ 's first appointee who preceded Salazar as Colorado Attorney General.
On January 20, 2009, Salazar was confirmed by unanimous consent in the Senate.

On January 16, 2013, it was reported that Salazar planned to resign his post as ___E:Secretary of the Interior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Interior)___ in March 2013, but his resignation was delayed pending Senate confirmation of his successor, ___E:Sally Jewell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sally_Jewell)___ .

On June 10, 2013, he became a partner in the major international law firm of ___E:WilmerHale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Cutler_Pickering_Hale_and_Dorr)___ , and was tasked with opening a Denver office for the firm.  On August 16, 2016, Salazar was appointed to head presidential candidate ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ 's transition team.

In May 2021, President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ nominated Salazar as the ___E:United States ambassador to Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Mexico)___ .

His nomination was confirmed by a ___E:voice vote U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_vote#United_States)___ in the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ on August 11, 2021.
Ken Salazar was born in ___E:Alamosa, Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alamosa,_Colorado)___ , the son of Emma Montoya and Enrique Salazar.
His elder brother is former Congressman ___E:John Salazar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Salazar)___ .

He grew up near ___E:Manassa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manassa,_Colorado)___ , in the community of Los Rincones in the ___E:San Luis Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Luis_Valley)___ area of south-central Colorado.

Salazar attended St. Francis Seminary and Centauri High School in ___E:La Jara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Jara,_Colorado)___ , graduating in 1973. He later attended ___E:Colorado College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_College)___ , earning a ___E:Bachelor of Arts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ degree in ___E:political science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science)___ in 1977, and received his ___E:Juris Doctor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor)___ from the ___E:University of Michigan Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School)___ in 1981. Later Salazar was awarded ___E:honorary degrees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_degree)___ (Doctor of Laws) from Colorado College (1993) and the ___E:University of Denver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Denver)___ (1999).
After graduating, Salazar started private law practice.

Salazar's ___E:Hispanic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic)___ roots trace back to the ___E:Hispanos of New Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanos_of_New_Mexico)___ before New Mexico and Colorado were split up when they became part of ___E:Southwestern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States)___ .

He has identified as a ___E:Mexican American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_American)___ saying, "I've been taunted, called names—from 'dirty Mexican' to lots of other names—as I was growing up, and even now as a United States Senator."
In 1986, Salazar became Chief Legal Counsel to then ___E:Colorado Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Governor)___ ___E:Roy Romer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Romer)___ .

In 1990, Romer appointed him to his ___E:Cabinet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_(government))___ as director of the ___E:Colorado Department of Natural Resources U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Department_of_Natural_Resources)___ .
In this position, he authored the Great Outdoors Colorado Amendment, which created a massive land conservation program of which he became chairman.
Salazar also created the Youth in Natural Resources program, giving thousands of Colorado's youth an opportunity to work and learn about Colorado's natural resources in public schools.

The Great Outdoors Colorado program's success was a model for ___E:President Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_Obama)___ 's America's Great Outdoors Initiative to create a 21st-century agenda for conservation and outdoor recreation.

In his cabinet role, he established reforms that forced mining and ___E:petroleum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum)___ operations to better protect the surrounding environment and helped plan and promote Denver's ___E:South Platte River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Platte_River)___ Valley redevelopment, transforming the area from an abandoned wasteland to a vibrant economic center.
In 1994, Salazar returned to private practice.

In 1998, he was elected state attorney general; he was reelected to this position in 2002. Police operations were streamlined under Salazar, and several new branches of law enforcement were created: the Gang Prosecution Unit, the Environmental Crimes Unit, and the General Fugitive Prosecutive Unit, which targeted murderers.

He also worked to strengthen consumer protection and anti- ___E:fraud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud)___ laws, as well as to protect children through new policy designed to crack down on ___E:sex offenders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_offender)___ .

As ___E:Colorado Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Attorney_General)___ , he also led numerous investigations, including into the 1999 ___E:Columbine High School massacre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbine_High_School_massacre)___ .
Salazar was awarded the Conference of Western Attorneys General Profile in Courage award for his work.
During Salazar's tenure, his office pursued several environmental cleanup cases around the state.

In a water contamination case involving the ___E:Summitville mine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summitville_mine)___ in ___E:Rio Grande County, Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande_County,_Colorado)___ , Salazar helped broker a joint settlement in which the federal and state government shared the $5 million settlement proceeds.
In ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_election_in_Colorado)___ , Salazar declared his candidacy for the U.S.

Senate seat being vacated by retiring ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Republican_Party)___ Senator ___E:Ben Nighthorse Campbell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Nighthorse_Campbell)___ .
Salazar considers himself a ___E:moderate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moderate)___ and has at times taken positions that are in disagreement with the base of his party.
He opposed ___E:gay adoption U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_adoption_in_the_United_States)___ for a number of years, although by 2004 he had reversed his position.
Salazar fell behind to candidate Mike Miles early in the state's caucus process.

The national Democratic Party backed Salazar with contributions from the DSCC, and Salazar came back to defeat Miles in the Democratic ___E:primary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ , going on to defeat ___E:beer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer)___ executive ___E:Pete Coors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Coors)___ of the ___E:Coors Brewing Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Brewing_Company)___ and win the ___E:general election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_election)___ for the Senate seat. He assumed office on January 3, 2005.

Salazar was a leading member of a bipartisan group of senators that developed the ___E:Comprehensive Immigration Reform Act of 2007 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_Immigration_Reform_Act_of_2007)___ , which would have provided a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and increased funding for border security, though the bill ultimately failed in the Senate.

During negotiations, Salazar was quoted by The New York Times saying he wanted the new point system to be equitable: "We do not want to create a system that is just for the wealthiest and most educated immigrants."

On May 23, 2005, Salazar was among the ___E:Gang of 14 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gang_of_14)___ moderate senators to forge a compromise on the Democrats' use of the ___E:filibuster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filibuster)___ against judicial appointments, thus blocking the Republican leadership's attempt to implement the so-called " ___E:nuclear option U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_option)___ ".

Under the agreement, the Democrats would retain the power to filibuster a Bush judicial nominee only in an "extraordinary circumstance", and the three most conservative Bush ___E:appellate court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellate_court)___ nominees ( ___E:Janice Rogers Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janice_Rogers_Brown)___ , ___E:Priscilla Owen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priscilla_Owen)___ and ___E:William Pryor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Pryor,_Jr.)___ ) would receive a vote by the full Senate.

Salazar has skirmished with ___E:Focus on the Family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_on_the_Family)___ , a Colorado-based ___E:conservative Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_right)___ group of national stature, over his stance on judicial nominees.

In 2005, Salazar voted against increasing fuel-efficiency standards ( ___E:CAFE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_Average_Fuel_Economy)___ ) for cars and trucks, a vote that the League of Conservation Voters believes is anti-environment.

In the same year, Salazar voted against an amendment to repeal tax breaks for ___E:ExxonMobil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExxonMobil)___ and other major ___E:petroleum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum)___ companies.

In August 2006, Ken Salazar supported fellow Democratic Senator ___E:Joe Lieberman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Lieberman)___ in his primary race against ___E:Ned Lamont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Lamont)___ in ___E:Connecticut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut)___ .
Lamont, running primarily as an ___E:anti-war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-war)___ candidate, won the primary.
Salazar's continued support of Lieberman, who successfully ran as an independent against Lamont, has rankled the anti-war wing of the Democratic Party.

In 2006, Salazar voted to end protections that limit ___E:offshore oil drilling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_oil_drilling)___ in ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ 's ___E:Gulf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ Coast.

Salazar introduced legislation, co-sponsored by Colorado Reps. ___E:John Salazar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Salazar)___ and ___E:Mark Udall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Udall)___ to limit ___E:natural gas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas)___ drilling on the environmentally-rich ___E:Roan Plateau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roan_Plateau)___ in western Colorado.
The bill increased the amount of acreage on the Plateau designated too environmentally sensitive to drill for gas.

Salazar worked in the Senate to give benefits to ___E:Rocky Flats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Flats)___ workers who became ill after working at the former nuclear weapons plant in Colorado.
The legislation would grant workers immediate access to medical coverage and compensation without the need to file individual health claims.

In 2007, Salazar was one of only a handful of Democrats to vote against a bill that would require the ___E:United States Army Corps of Engineers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Corps_of_Engineers)___ to consider ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ when planning water projects.

Salazar received a 25 percent vote rating for 2007 by the ___E:Humane Society of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humane_Society_of_the_United_States)___ ,  a zero percent vote rating for 2005–2006 by ___E:Fund for Animals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fund_for_Animals)___ ,  a 60 percent vote rating for 2007 by ___E:Defenders of Wildlife U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defenders_of_Wildlife)___ ,  and a zero percent vote rating on the ___E:Animal Welfare Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Welfare_Institute)___ Compassion Index.

He also supported the Bush administration's release of lands in the ___E:Conservation Reserve Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_Reserve_Program)___ (CRP) for emergency haying in Colorado's ___E:Yuma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuma_County,_Colorado)___ and ___E:Phillips Counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phillips_County,_Colorado)___ .

Salazar has an 81 percent lifetime rating from the ___E:League of Conservation Voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Conservation_Voters)___ , including a 100 percent rating for the year 2008.

Salazar resigned his Senate seat on January 20, 2009, upon his confirmation by the Senate to become ___E:Secretary of the Interior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Interior)___ under ___E:President Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .
Salazar accepted Obama's offer to join his cabinet as the Secretary of the Interior.
His appointment triggered a ___E:Saxbe fix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxbe_fix)___ by Congress.

On January 7, 2009, Congress approved a bill, ___E:S.J.Res. 3 U:(https://www.congress.gov/bill/111th-congress/senate-joint-resolution/3)___ , and President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ signed it into law, providing such a fix by reducing the Secretary of Interior's salary to the level it was prior to the time Salazar took office in January 2009.
The Senate confirmed Salazar's nomination by voice vote on January 20, 2009, shortly after Obama was sworn in as president.

As Secretary of the Interior, Salazar was in charge of the ___E:National Park Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Park_Service)___ , the ___E:Bureau of Land Management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Land_Management)___ , the ___E:United States Fish and Wildlife Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Fish_and_Wildlife_Service)___ , the ___E:United States Geological Survey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey)___ , the ___E:Bureau of Indian Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Affairs)___ , and other federal agencies overseen by the Interior Department.

Salazar was one of two Hispanics serving in Obama's Cabinet, along with ___E:Secretary of Labor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Labor)___ ___E:Hilda Solis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilda_Solis)___ of ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ .

Salazar is the second Hispanic Interior Secretary after ___E:Manuel Lujan, Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Lujan,_Jr.)___ , who held the post from 1989 to 1993 under President ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ .

As secretary of the department, Salazar began a large-scale effort within the department to ensure that the country's ___E:national parks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_parks)___ and national monuments were inclusive of America's tribal and minority communities.

Salazar worked to create new monuments to honor ___E:Cesar Chavez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesar_Chavez)___ , the ___E:Buffalo Soldiers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Soldiers)___ , ___E:Harriet Tubman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harriet_Tubman)___ and the ___E:Underground Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underground_Railroad)___ , ___E:Fort Monroe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Monroe)___ and sacred Native American sites like ___E:Chimney Rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimney_Rock_National_Monument)___ in Colorado.

Several prominent environmentalist groups were wary of Salazar, noting his strong ties with the coal and mining industries. ___E:Kieran Suckling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kieran_Suckling)___ , executive director of Center for Biological Diversity, which tracks endangered species and habitat issues stated, "He [Ken Salazar] is a right-of-center Democrat who often favors industry and big ___E:agriculture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture)___ in battles over ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ , ___E:fuel efficiency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel_efficiency)___ and ___E:endangered species U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_species)___ ."

The nomination was praised, however, by ___E:Gene Karpinski U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Karpinski)___ , President of the ___E:League of Conservation Voters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Conservation_Voters)___ .

Upon the nomination, Karpinski said, "Throughout his career, Senator Salazar has campaigned on a pledge of support for 'our land, our water, our people.' With a perfect 100% score on the 2008 LCV Scorecard, he has lived up to that pledge.
As a westerner, Senator Salazar has hands on experience with land and water issues, and will restore the Department of the Interior's role as the steward of America's public resources.
We look forward to working with him to protect the health of America's land, water, and people in the coming years."

Although Senate Republicans were expected to raise questions concerning Salazar's stances on ___E:oil shale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_shale)___ development and drilling in environmentally sensitive areas,  Salazar was one of several Obama Cabinet appointees confirmed in the Senate by voice vote on January 20, 2009, shortly after Obama's inauguration.
Salazar became the 50th Secretary of the Interior succeeding ___E:Dirk Kempthorne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Kempthorne)___ , who praised Salazar's appointment.

Colorado ___E:Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Colorado)___ ___E:Bill Ritter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Ritter)___ appointed Denver Superintendent of Schools ___E:Michael Bennet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bennet)___ to finish Salazar's term in the Senate, which expired in January 2011.
On January 23, 2009, Salazar stated that he was considering reopening the ___E:Statue of Liberty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty)___ 's crown to tourists.

The crown has been closed to the public since the September 11, 2001 attacks. "I hope we can find a way", Salazar said in a statement. "It would proclaim to the world—both figuratively and literally—that the path to the light of liberty is open to all."

On March 6, 2009, Salazar agreed to move forward with the ___E:Fish and Wildlife Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_and_Wildlife_Service)___ 's decision to remove the ___E:Rocky Mountain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountain)___ ___E:gray wolf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray_wolf)___ from the ___E:Endangered Species List U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_Species_List)___ in ___E:Montana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana)___ and ___E:Idaho U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho)___ , but not ___E:Wyoming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming)___ .

Minimum recovery goal for wolves in the northern Rocky Mountains is at least 30 breeding pairs and at least 300 wolves for at least three consecutive years, a goal that was attained in 2002 and has been exceeded every year since. (There are currently about 95 breeding pairs and 1,600 wolves in Montana, Idaho, and Wyoming.)  Salazar, a former rancher has come under criticism of groups like the ___E:Defenders of Wildlife U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defenders_of_Wildlife)___ for this decision, and lack of protection of wolves.

On May 9, 2009, Salazar announced the upholding of a Bush-era policy that prevents the regulation of ___E:greenhouse gas emissions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions)___ via the ___E:Endangered Species Act (ESA) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_Species_Act)___ , a policy he pledged to reevaluate when he took office in January.

The policy states that, despite the apparent negative impact ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ has on ___E:polar bears U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_bears)___ , an endangered species, greenhouse gasses cannot be regulated with the ESA. Salazar stated in a conference call announcing the decision that "The single greatest threat to the polar bear is the melting of Arctic Sea ice due to climate change," but the Endangered Species Act "is not the appropriate tool for us to deal with what is a global issue." The decision was met with criticism from environmental groups and praise from energy groups including the ___E:American Petroleum Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Petroleum_Institute)___ , some Democrats and many Republicans.

Salazar contended in the same conference call that the ESA was never intended to be used for the regulation of climate change, while sidestepping questions of how this situation is different from that of the Clean Air Act, which is being used by the ___E:Environmental Protection Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency)___ to regulate emissions.

In May 2009, ___E:Colorado Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Colorado)___ ___E:Bill Ritter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Ritter)___ , and the state's both senators, Michael Bennet and Mark Udall, wrote a letter to President Obama, recommending Salazar be appointed to the ___E:Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ following the resignation of ___E:David Souter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Souter)___ .

Salazar stated on the ___E:Today U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_(American_TV_program))___ that he was not interested and enjoyed his current job.  ___E:United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit Judge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Second_Circuit)___ ___E:Sonia Sotomayor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_Sotomayor)___ was eventually ___E:nominated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_Sotomayor_Supreme_Court_nomination)___ and confirmed.

With Ritter's announcement on January 6, 2010, that he would not seek re-election as governor,  speculation began to swirl about a possible Salazar candidacy ___E:that year U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Colorado_gubernatorial_election)___ .

Congressman ___E:John Salazar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Salazar)___ , Salazar's brother, told local media that he thought his brother would likely run for governor. ___E:Denver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver,_Colorado)___ Mayor ___E:John Hickenlooper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hickenlooper)___ indicated that while he was considering a run himself, he would "do everything [he could] to help him get elected."  Both the Secretary's brother, John, and the ___E:Obama administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_administration)___ urged him to run for governor,  but he ultimately declined and endorsed Hickenlooper's campaign.

On April 28, 2010, Ken Salazar approved ___E:Cape Wind U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Wind)___ ,   the first-ever commercial wind operation in public water, leading to initiation of the approval process for the first-of-its-kind Atlantic wind energy transmission line.

During his time as secretary, Salazar successfully developed and implemented numerous renewable energy initiatives on public lands and helped lead the Obama administration's "all of the above" energy strategy.

Secretary Salazar prioritized the rapid, responsible development of ___E:renewable energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy)___ on America's public lands, greenlighting the development of over 11,000 megawatts of renewable energy on public lands, including approval of the first-ever ___E:solar energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_energy)___ projects on public lands, and creation of the first-ever roadmap for future solar energy development in the West.

During Salazar's tenure, the department also undertook new surveys to evaluate and identify innovative capacity and efficiency increases to help enhance ___E:hydropower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydropower)___ generation at facilities of the ___E:Bureau of Reclamation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Reclamation)___ , the nation's second-largest hydropower producer.
He has dealt with criticism after pushing to impose tougher leasing rules and cancel a series of planned drilling operations in ___E:Alaska U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska)___ and elsewhere.

Salazar has dealt with criticism over his handling of the ___E:Deepwater Horizon oil spill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepwater_Horizon_oil_spill)___ , both because of the way his agency handled the permitting process for underwater drilling, and also because of the way the aftermath of the spill has been handled by the government.

But Salazar also ushered in the most comprehensive offshore oil and gas safety initiatives and reforms ever in the United States, overhauling the government's antiquated and conflicted offshore oil and gas management program while approving millions of acres for oil and gas development offshore.
Salazar also implemented a new five-year plan for responsible ___E:oil and gas exploration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocarbon_exploration)___ and development in America's offshore waters.
In May 2010 Salazar testified to Congress that he had issued a "hit the pause button" order and that no new permits had been issued since the Deepwater Horizon explosion in the Gulf of Mexico.

However, a new deepwater well had been started in the Gulf since April 20, and the Department of the Interior under Salazar had "issued permits for at least seventeen other new offshore oil projects."
